content:
Hello,

This mainly discussion for Lean FRO Std Library maintainers.

The topic is about HTTP Header parsing.

In Http, it's common to process headers even outside the Http enveloppe. The main example is for all the "multiplart/" media types that also embbed standard headers with exactly the same grammar as HTTP.

For LeanIO, i added support for "multipart/form-data" media type.
But it's also common in batching HTTP request with "mulipart/mixed" (a poors man multiplexing capability on HTTP1.1 or for Email attachments)

But since the parsing logic for headers is interleaved with the full H1 state machine, this part is unfortunately not reusable.

I essentially rolled my own Headers parser, but i think it would be nice if this part of the state machine could be independent somehow, so i could reuse it without duplicating an already good implementation.

Is this something that could be possible ? what do you think ?

Your post is a bit vague. Could you say more precisely which part of the functionality you would want to be extracted out? Is it only docs#Std.Http.Protocol.H1.parseSingleHeader that you want to be a public API or do you want more than that?

It would be nice if the part that extracts the full headers (interleaved in H1, so not a in a single function today) could be made independent and public. For the parseSingleHeader, i can already access it directly actually.
You can see the machinery in processNeedHeader and processRead.
The issue about extracting this would be that it would need refactoring from a monolithic H1 state machine into a modularized state machine, and this is maybe be too much of a refactoring for such a small feature.
Yeah, I think this is in the "feel free to open an RFC, but don't expect us to act on it in the short term" category.
